# Seen 1.1.1 — security patch

Prepared as a pre-release candidate for test-environment acceptance. Plugin ID: `ru.internal.mattermost.seen`.

Seen gives message authors a list of users whose active client viewport displayed the message. **Viewed does not guarantee that a person read or understood the message.**

## Changes

- Updated Go 1.26.7 → 1.26.9 and golang.org/x/net 0.58.0 → 0.60.0 to address the fixable dependency advisories found in the 2026-10-10 review; updated matching indirect Go modules.
- Pinned the release compiler and govulncheck 1.9.0. Security checks cover source and both packaged Linux binaries, module integrity and npm audit.
- Retained Go symbols for artifact analysis while omitting DWARF debug information and local source paths; moved temporary packaging outside the checkout.
- Preserved backend/frontend runtime source, receipt API/KV format, first-view timestamp, deduplication, viewport rules and plugin ID.
- Retained profile-based names, Today/Yesterday/date labels, compact double checks, five-viewer preview and Show all/full-list dialog.

The install asset must match the previously audited 1.1.1 package:

`SHA256 2ffd56064bf65d9969e6aa6d96533f5deb274e78e73a5e2336cf4aa46233e9ea`

## Validation and limits

Local validation on 2026-10-11 passed Go race tests/vet, frontend formatting/lint/typecheck, 24 unit tests, mock-host Chromium smoke, clean reproducible build, module integrity and source secret scanning. govulncheck reported zero symbol and imported-package findings for source and both Linux binaries; npm audit reported zero findings at that time. GitHub Actions repeats the build, browser and security gates before preparing this draft; see the linked commit's Actions run for its actual results.

GO-2026-5932 remains a module-level advisory for the unmaintained x/crypto/openpgp package. OpenPGP is not imported or compiled into the plugin. No scanner allowlist is used; this does not claim that OpenPGP itself has been fixed.

Live Mattermost gateway/authz/CSRF, the T01–T35 acceptance matrix, and two-node HA/failover/load validation remain pending. Mock and unit tests do not replace those checks. Message deletion cleanup is best effort during KV outages; user/channel erasure and backup retention remain separate operational concerns. This candidate does not claim production or HA certification.

## Installation

Target: Mattermost 11.10.x, Linux amd64/arm64, Web/Desktop. Mobile and Connected Workspaces receipts are not supported.

1. Verify the asset checksum, record current settings and confirm a current backup. Disable Seen before updating; update all app nodes together.
2. Upload **`ru.internal.mattermost.seen-1.1.1.tar.gz`** through System Console plugin management as an update of the existing ID. Confirm version 1.1.1, settings and activation, then reload clients.
3. Run the live acceptance checks described in the bundled `docs/release-1.1.1.md`, `docs/testing.md` and `docs/operations.md` before wider use.

With both assets and the checksum file in one directory:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-1.1.1-github.txt
```

The `-github.zip` source asset includes the publication workflow from the tagged commit. It differs from the earlier local source ZIP; the installation tar.gz is unchanged. Source ZIPs are not installation packages.

For security rollback, disable Seen until a compatible fixed package is available. Returning to 1.1.0 returns the dependency advisories; do not delete Plugin KV as a routine rollback.

Portions of this project were generated or refactored with assistance from OpenAI Codex.
